shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures turned higher on Thursday as traders adjusted positions ahead of Friday's widely anticipated U.S. Department of Agriculture supply and demand report.

children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures turned higher on Thursday as traders adjusted positions ahead of Friday's widely anticipated U.S. Department of Agriculture supply and demand report.
The USDA's supply-and-demand forecasts are awaited as an indicator of the extent to which hot, dry spells this summer hurt U.S. Midwest crops such as soybeans.
In a Reuters poll, analysts on average predict that the USDA will estimate corn yield for the month at 178.2 bushels per acre.
On Tuesday, the USDA estimated that 56% of the corn crop was in good-to-excellent condition, down 1 percentage point from the previous week but in line with average analyst expectations.
The eastern part of the U.S. Midwest will trend drier in the coming weeks, aiding the harvest, according to forecaster Commodity Weather Group.
settled 6 cents higher at $5.33-3/4 per bushel.
